fact: Five people were bitten in twelve days along the Jersey Shore in 1916
source: Close to Shore: The Terrifying Shark Attacks of 1916, Michael Capuzzo (2001)

fact: Attacks occurred eleven miles inland on a tidal creek (Matawan Creek)
source: Close to Shore: The Terrifying Shark Attacks of 1916, Michael Capuzzo (2001)

fact: Experts at the time believed a great white shark could not survive in freshwater creeks
source: Close to Shore: The Terrifying Shark Attacks of 1916, Michael Capuzzo (2001); contemporary statements by scientists including Frederic Lucas of the American Museum of Natural History

fact: Four people died in the series of attacks
source: Jersey Shore shark attacks of 1916, Wikipedia (sourced from multiple historical accounts)

fact: Matawan Creek was approximately sixteen feet wide at the attack sites
source: Close to Shore: The Terrifying Shark Attacks of 1916, Michael Capuzzo (2001)

fact: Beaches across the eastern seaboard were closed following the attacks
source: Close to Shore: The Terrifying Shark Attacks of 1916, Michael Capuzzo (2001); widely documented in contemporary newspaper accounts from July 1916
